title: The ancient question of rational solutions
mathematical_role: Connect the congruent-number example, the elliptic curve E_5, rational points, and the limits of finite search.
learning_objective: Distinguish literal arithmetic data from visual analogy and recognize how a verified rational point on E_5 corresponds to a rational right triangle of area five.
literal_semantics: The predecessor names the equation y^2 = x^3 - 25x and intends to connect it to rational points and the area-five congruent-number example.
nonliteral_semantics: The drawn cubic is not a verified plot of y^2 = x^3 - 25x.
The displayed point locations are not verified rational coordinates unless separately labeled.
The triangle proportions are not the exact 3/2, 20/3, 41/6 triangle.
The lower search constellation is illustrative and not a completeness computation.

notes: The successor should use E_5: y^2=x^3-25x, the verified point (25/4,75/8), and the rational triangle with sides 3/2, 20/3, 41/6.

reproducibility_notes: The predecessor is illustrative rather than generated from the stated elliptic curve and rational-point data.

accessibility.alt_text: An illustrated map from rational right triangles and cubic curves to sparse rational points, torsion, rank, and the limits of finite search.
accessibility.long_description: The predecessor compresses exact arithmetic into an illustrated panorama. The successor must make the curve geometry and selected rational coordinates literal, label the exact area-five triangle, and keep the inability of finite search to certify the complete Mordell-Weil group explicit.

claim_boundary.strongest_visual_claim: Pedagogical exposition of a source-stated exact congruent-number example and the distinction between finding rational points and proving completeness.
not_claimed: The rank of every elliptic curve

supersession_reason: The conceptual role is sound, but literal arithmetic should be rendered from the stated exact curve and verified rational data.
